# Load 1000 Genomes

```{r}
g1000 <- gt_load("../data/raw/data_input/1000_Genomes_b37_clean.gt")

# append population info
pop_table <- read.table("../data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable",
  sep = "\t", fill = TRUE
)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2", "FID", "Population", "V5", "V6", "V7")

pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table, pop_table$IID %in% g1000$id)

matching_m <- match(g1000$id, pop_table_sub$IID)
g1000$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m),
  pop_table_sub$V2[matching_m],
  g1000$population
)

cdx <- g1000 %>% filter(population == "CDX")

if (
  file.exists(
    "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_no_ld_cdx.gt"
  )
) {
  file.remove(
    "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_no_ld_cdx.gt"
  )
  file.remove(
    "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_no_ld_cdx.bk"
  )
  file.remove(
    "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_no_ld_cdx.rds"
  )
}

mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo <- rbind(
  mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo,
  cdx,
  as_is = FALSE, flip_strand = TRUE,
  use_position = TRUE, quiet = FALSE,
  backingfile = "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_no_ld_cdx"
```

# Create a second dataset with Merina labelled separately

```{r sep_merina, message = FALSE}
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population <-
  as.character(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population)

# load supervised admixture results
qmats <- read_q_files("../data/intermediate/admixture")
# add id to individuals
fam <- read.table(
  "../data/intermediate/admixture/admixture_supervised_subset.fam",
  header = FALSE
)
qmats$id <- fam$V2

# load gt that admixture results were calculated from
mad_bor_g1000_sum <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_clean_ld.gt")

# subset mad_bor_g1000_sum to only individuals in qmats$id
mad_bor_g1000_sum_sub <- mad_bor_g1000_sum %>%
  filter(id %in% qmats$id)

# tidy with the gt
mad_bor_g1000_sum_sub <- augment(get_q_matrix(qmats, k = 2, run = 1),
  data = mad_bor_g1000_sum_sub
)

# filter to merina
merina <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_sub %>% filter(population == "Merina")

# find which .Q column represents Asian ancestry
asian_ancestry_q <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_sub %>%
  filter(population == "Borneo") %>%
  # Get median value of Q1 and Q2
  summarise(.Q1 = median(.Q1), .Q2 = median(.Q2)) %>%
  # Pivot in order to subset
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(".Q1", ".Q2"),
    names_to = "column_name",
    values_to = "median_val"
  ) %>%
  # Find the row with the max value
  slice_max(median_val, n = 1) %>%
  # get the column name
  pull(column_name)


# split groups
# split groups
merina$population <- ifelse(merina %>% select(all_of(asian_ancestry_q)) > 0.5,
  "MerinaA",
  "MerinaB"
)
merina <- merina[, c("id", "population")]
merina$id <- sub("RR.*", "", merina$id)

# match mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$id and merina$id and replace the population
# column in mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam with the population column in merina
matching_m <- match(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$id, merina$id)
mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m),
  merina$population[matching_m], mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population
)

# count number of MerinaA
cat(
  "Merina group > 0.5",
  length(which(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population == "MerinaA"))
)
cat(
  "Merina group < 0.5",
  length(which(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population == "MerinaB"))
)

mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population <-
  as.factor(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam$population)

write.table(mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_fam,
  "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.fam",
  row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, sep = " ", quote = FALSE
)

file.copy(
  "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.bed",
  "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.bed",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
file.copy(
  "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.bim",
  "../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.bim",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

# Write .par files for MALDER

```{r write_par, message = FALSE}
# First, with Merina together
admix_list <- c(
  "Betsileo", "Betsimisaraka", "Diego", "Mikea",
  "Sakalava_Tsimihety", "Temoro", "Vezo", "Merina"
)

# Fixed parameters
geno <-
  "../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.geno"
snp <-
  "../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.snp"
ind <-
  "../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo.ind"
ref_str <- list("Borneo;Sumba;Dai;Esan;Yoruba;Mozambique_Chopi")

# Root output directory (do NOT modify inside the loop)
base_root <- "s07_MALDER_par_files"

write_par_files <- function(base_root,
                            admix_list,
                            ref_str,
                            geno,
                            snp,
                            ind) {
  # for (refset in refpop_list) {
  for (admix in admix_list) {

    # Final output directory for this refpop set
    base_out <- file.path(getwd(), base_root) # , folder

    # Filename for the .par file
    outfile <- sprintf(
      "%s/s07b_malder_%s.par",
      base_out, tolower(admix)
    )
    file.create(outfile)

    # Write the .par file content
    par_text <- paste0(
      "genotypename: ", geno, "\n",
      "snpname: ", snp, "\n",
      "indivname: ", ind, "\n",
      "checkmap: YES\n",
      "jackknife: YES\n",
      "mindis: 0.005\n",
      "admixpop: ", admix, "\n",
      "refpops: ", ref_str, "\n",
      "raw_outname: ", file.path(
        base_out,
        paste0("malder_", tolower(admix), ".txt")
      ), "\n"
    )

    writeLines(par_text, con = outfile)
  }
  # }
}

write_par_files(
  base_root,
  admix_list,
  ref_str,
  geno,
  snp,
  ind
)

# And then for split Merina
path <- "../../data/intermediate/rbind_data/rbind_sort_dist/"
geno <-
  paste0(path, "mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.geno")
snp <-
  paste0(path, "mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.snp")
ind <-
  paste0(path, "mad_bor_g1000_sum_neo_sep.ind")

admix_list <- c("MerinaA", "MerinaB")

write_par_files(
  base_root,
  admix_list,
  ref_str,
  geno,
  snp,
  ind
)
```

## Mindis parameter notes

mindis: 0.005 - minimum genetic distance (in Morgans) at which to start
curve fitting (default: determined using LD correlation).
<https://comppopgenworkshop2019.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents/06_alder/alder.html>
States that the default calculates the correlation in LD decay between
the target and each reference, and uses 'the minimum distance that shows
no correlation in both references.' 'If it continues beyond 2 cM (due to
either a strong bottleneck or admixture in a reference), the program
aborts.'

If mindis is automatically chosen, some runs fail with:
'too much long-range LD; not plotting LD curve'
'fit start = inf because of long-range LD correlation; exiting'

For Borneo-Esan, the failing runs are Betsileo and Merina/Merina A.
This is likely due to strong bottleneck in Asian ancestry component, given that
it fails only for populations with a larger Asian ancestry component.

Dai-Esan is successful for all populations, regardless of mindis setting.

## Other parameters

checkmap: YES
binsize: 0.0005 default - genetic distance resolution (in
Morgans) - the size of bins that MALDER splits the genome up into, used
to calculate the distance between the bins of two snps as opposed to the
distance between the each individual pair of snps, for computational
efficiency
jackknife: YES - outputs results from leave-one-chromosome-out jackknifing

# Run bash scripts in a loop

```{bash run_malder, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
CODE_ROOT=~/Git/malagasy_diversity/code/s07_MALDER_par_files
RESULT_ROOT=~/Git/malagasy_diversity/results/s07_MALDER

for file in "$CODE_ROOT"/*/; do

    # Strip path and trailing slash
    BASENAME=$(basename "$file")

    echo "Processing reference set: $BASENAME"

    # Make matching output directory
    OUTDIR="$RESULT_ROOT/$BASENAME"
    mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

    # Enter the folder containing the .par files
    cd "$CODE_ROOT" || continue

    # Loop through each .par file
    for PAR in *.par; do
        LOG="$OUTDIR/${PAR%.par}.log"

        echo "  Running MALDER on $PAR"
        malder -p "$PAR" > "$LOG" 2>&1
    done

    echo "Finished $BASENAME"
    echo "----------------------"
done

```

# Check for multiple admixture events

malder begins by assuming a single wave of admixture, then:

"1. Add a new exponential term to the model.
2. Fit the model by alternately optimizing all exponential decay terms and amplitudes.
3. Calculate standard errors on all terms using a jackknife.
4. If all decay terms have a p-value less than 0.01, go back to step 1, otherwise finish. " Pickrell et al. 2014

Sources of admixture at each wave can then be inferred if multiple waves are present.

malder README at https://github.com/joepickrell/malder states: 'The output will be printed to the screen, with lines starting with RESULT_X being the results from fitting X curves to the data. The program will always fit one more curve than is necessary, so if you get RESULT_3, then the lines that start with RESULT_2 are the ones you're interested in.'

Therefore, a RESULT_2 across log files indicates a single wave is best fit, while RESULT_3 indicates multiple waves.

```{r}
# check for any 'RESULT_3' in the log files
# this would indicate multiple admixture events
res_folders <- list.dirs("../results/s07_MALDER",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = FALSE
)

get_logs <- function(res_folders) {
  files <- c()
  for (folder in res_folders) {
    new_logs <- list.files(folder,
      pattern = ".log",
      full.names = TRUE
    )
    files <- c(files, new_logs)
  }
  return(files)
}

files <- get_logs(res_folders)



# remove any from files that don't have 'malder' in  the name
files <- files[grepl("_malder", files)]

# use readLines to read each of files
logs <- lapply(files, readLines)

# check for 'RESULT_3' in each log file
multiple_admix <- sapply(
  logs,
  function(log_file) {
    any(grepl("^RESULT_3",
      log_file,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    ))
  }
)

if (any(multiple_admix)) {
  cat("Some populations show evidence of multiple admixture events:\n")
  print(files[multiple_admix])
} else {
  cat("No populations show evidence of multiple admixture events.\n")
}
```

# Get and process outputs

```{r process_outputs, message = FALSE}
# Extract "DATA:" lines from each log file in the list
data_lines <- lapply(
  logs,
  function(log_file) {
    log_file[grepl("^DATA:",
      log_file,
      ignore.case = TRUE
    )]
  }
)

data_lines <- unlist(data_lines)
colnames <- data_lines[1]
# find list elements with "p-value" in them and remove them
data_lines <- data_lines[!grepl("p-value", data_lines)]
split_data <- lapply(data_lines, function(x) strsplit(x, "\t")[[1]])
result <- do.call(rbind, split_data)
result <- as.data.frame(result, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# remove first column
result <- result[, -1]

colnames(result) <- c(
  "test_res", "p_value", "test_pop",
  "ref A", "ref B", "2-ref z-score",
  "2-ref decay", "2-ref amp_exp"
)

# # split $`2-ref decay` into 2 columns
split_dates <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(result$`2-ref decay`, " "))
# # remove the middle column
split_dates <- split_dates[, -2]
# # add column names
colnames(split_dates) <- c("admixture_date", "CI")
# # turn into a dataframe
split_dates <- as.data.frame(split_dates)
# # make numeric
split_dates$admixture_date <- as.numeric(split_dates$admixture_date)
split_dates$CI <- as.numeric(split_dates$CI)
result <- cbind(result, split_dates)

# split $`2-ref amp_exp` into 2 columns
split_amp <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(result$`2-ref amp_exp`, " "))
# remove the middle column
split_amp <- split_amp[, -2]
# add column names
colnames(split_amp) <- c("amp_exp", "amp_exp_CI")
# turn into a dataframe
split_amp <- as.data.frame(split_amp)
# make numeric
split_amp$amp_exp <- as.numeric(split_amp$amp_exp)
split_amp$amp_exp_CI <- as.numeric(split_amp$amp_exp_CI)
result <- cbind(result, split_amp)


# # Process each log file
log_text <- function(log) {
  # Find line beginning "Computing 2-ref weighted LD with weights"
  header_index <- grep("Computing 2-ref weighted LD with weights", log)

  test_pop_index <- grep("admixpop:", log)

  # find test pop
  test_pop <- sub(".*admixpop:", "", log[test_pop_index][1])

  out <- vector("list", length(header_index))


  for (k in seq_along(header_index)) {
    start <- header_index[k]
    end <-
      if (k < length(header_index)) header_index[k + 1] - 1 else length(log)

    block <- log[start:end]

    # Search for 'amp_aff:'
    amp_aff_line <- grep(
      "amp_aff:",
      block,
      value = TRUE
    )

    amp_aff <- if (length(amp_aff_line) == 0) {
      NA
    } else {
      as.numeric(
        sub(
          "[[:space:]]+\\+/-.*", "",
          sub(".*amp_aff:[[:space:]]*", "", amp_aff_line[1])
        )
      )
    }

    # find the two population names after
    # "Computing 2-ref weighted LD with weights..."
    refs <- sub(".*weights", "", log[header_index][k])

    out[[k]] <- data.frame(
      test_pop = test_pop,
      refs = refs,
      amp_aff = amp_aff,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }


  return(out)
}


amp_aff_lines <- lapply(logs, log_text)

unlist1 <- unlist(amp_aff_lines, recursive = FALSE)
amp_aff_data <- do.call(rbind, unlist1)

# split amp_aff_data$refs into ref A and ref B
refs_split <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(amp_aff_data$refs, " "))
amp_aff_data$ref1 <- refs_split[, 2]
amp_aff_data$ref2 <- refs_split[, 3]
# strip whitespace from amp_aff_data$test_pop
amp_aff_data$test_pop <- trimws(amp_aff_data$test_pop)
amp_aff_data$ref1 <- trimws(amp_aff_data$ref1)
amp_aff_data$ref2 <- trimws(amp_aff_data$ref2)

# same order
testthat::expect_equal(result$test_pop, amp_aff_data$test_pop)
testthat::expect_equal(result$`ref A`, amp_aff_data$ref1)
testthat::expect_equal(result$`ref B`, amp_aff_data$ref2)

result$amp_aff <- as.numeric(amp_aff_data$amp_aff)

result$test_pop <- factor(result$test_pop,
  levels = c(
    "Betsimisaraka", "Temoro", "MerinaB",
    "Betsileo", "Mikea", "Merina",
    "Sakalava_Tsimihety", "Vezo", "MerinaA",
    "Diego"
  )
)

# # save result
saveRDS(result, "../results/s07_MALDER/malder_results_all.RDS")
```

'Also note that we do not use the jackknife to
   estimate bias: i.e., for any inference of the form "x +/- y", x is
   computed using data from all chromosomes and y is the standard
   error obtained from the jackknife.' README file for MALDER

```{r}
  !(
    (result$`ref A` %in% c("Esan", "Yoruba", "Mozambique_Chopi")) &
      (result$`ref B` %in% c("Esan", "Yoruba", "Mozambique_Chopi"))
  )
)

# remove results with two Asian references
result <- subset(
  result,
  !(
    (result$`ref A` %in% c("Borneo", "Sumba", "Dai")) &
      (result$`ref B` %in% c("Borneo", "Sumba", "Dai"))
  )
)
```

# Example LD curve plots

'Weighted LD curves computed on real populations often exhibit a nonzero
horizontal asymptote contrary to the exact exponential decay formulas we
have derived above. Such behavior can be caused by assortative mating
resulting in subpopulations structured by ancestry percentage in
violation of our model. We show in Appendix A that if we instead model
the admixed population as consisting of randomly mating subpopulations
with heterogeneous amounts α—now a random variable—of mixed ancestry,
our equations for the curves take the form' (Loh et al 2013)

$$
E[a(d)] = M e^{-nd} + K
$$

'We fit discretized weighted LD curves as from Equation 9, using
least-squares to find best-fit parameters.' (Loh et al 2013)

'the affine term K...arises from the presence of subpopulations with differing ancestry percentages'. 

The following plotting code is adapted from
<https://comppopgenworkshop2019.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents/06_alder/alder.html>
Which describes as: E[Y] = M times e \ ^-nd + K

Adjusting the parameters ref_a and ref_b will print all LD curves for this combination.

```{r plot_curves}
result <- readRDS("../results/s07_MALDER/malder_results_all.RDS")

files <- list.files("../code/s07_MALDER_par_files",
  pattern = ".txt",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = FALSE
)


plot_curves <- function(ref_a, ref_b, files, result) {
  result_sub <- subset(
    result,
    result$`ref A` == ref_a & result$`ref B` == ref_b
  )

  ref_combo <- paste0(ref_a, ";", ref_b)

  counter <- 1
  plot_list <- list()

  for (i in files) {
    d1 <- read.table(i, header = FALSE)
    colnames(d1) <- d1[1, ]
    d1 <- d1[-1, ]

    n <- result_sub[counter, ]$admixture_date # decay - estimated admixture date
    M <- result_sub[counter, ]$amp_exp # amp_exp -
    K <- result_sub[counter, ]$amp_aff # amp_aff -

    # xv is distance between SNP bins (cM) - genetic distance
    xv <- 100 * as.numeric(d1$d)
    weightedLD_col <- which(colnames(d1) == ref_combo)

    names(d1)[weightedLD_col] <- "weightedLD"

    prdv <- M * exp(-1 * n * xv / 100) + K # E[Y] = M times e^-nd + K

    this_plot <- ggplot(
      d1,
      aes(
        x = d, y = as.numeric(weightedLD),
        group = counter
      )
    ) +
      geom_point(color = "blue", shape = 4) +
      geom_line(aes(y = prdv), color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
      labs(
        x = "Genetic distance (cM)",
        y = "Weighted LD",
        title = paste(
          "Weighted LD decay curve for",
          result_sub[counter, ]$test_pop
        )
      ) +
      theme_minimal()

    plot_list[[counter]] <- this_plot
    counter <- counter + 1
  }
  return(plot_list)
}

# # Run the function
ref_a <- "Borneo"
ref_b <- "Mozambique_Chopi"
res <- plot_curves(ref_a, ref_b, files, result)
#
for (p in res) print(p)
```

## Recording R environment

Part of ensuring our workflow is reproducible is to keep track of the R
environment. We will automatically save our R environment into a file
called `r_environment.json`.

```{r save-r-environment, echo=FALSE, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
filename_rmd <- "s07_MALDER.Rmd"
filename_renv <- paste0(
  res_dir, "/renv_",
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(filename_rmd)),
  ".json"
)
renv::lockfile_write(renv::lockfile_create(), file = filename_renv)
```
